questions: Is the main reason for your visit a tremor or shaking in your hands?
Does the tremor occur when your hands are completely at rest, such as resting on a table?
Is the tremor noticeably worse on one side of your body than the other?
Have you noticed that your movements have become slower than they used to be?
Do you feel any stiffness or rigidity in your arms or legs?
Do you have any difficulty with your balance when standing or walking?
Does drinking alcohol temporarily make the tremor better?
Do any of your close family members have a similar tremor?
Are you currently taking any prescription medications?
Do you have a history of thyroid problems?
Have you noticed if your handwriting has become smaller or more cramped?
Have you had any recent infections or fevers?
orders: Bedside examination of cerebellar function, including finger-to-nose testing and rapid alternating movements.
Testing for subtle parkinsonian signs using Froment's maneuver and repetitive finger tapping.
Detailed examination for dystonia, including observation during sustained arm elevation and writing.
Objective assessment of gait, including tandem walking.
